# Adjudication Task — Chapter 676

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃676화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|화염신장으로부터 시작된 화염은, 애뇌산의 초입에서 시작되어 삽시간에 사방으로 번졌다.
  6|
  7|화륵. 콰아아아!
  8|
  9|불교에서 말하는 초열지옥(焦熱地獄)이 있다면 이런 광경이 아닐까 싶다.
 10|
 11|쉴 새 없이 흩날리는 잿가루와 매캐한 연기. 그리고 파도처럼 넘실거리며 모든 것을 집어삼키는 화마(火魔).
 12|
 13|투둑, 구구구궁!
 14|
 15|줄지어 쓰러지는 거목에 지축이 흔들리고 산새들이 일제히 날아오른다.
 16|
 17|산림 보호 협회 명예 회장인 적천강이 봤다면 눈을 까뒤집을 만한 광경이었지만, 다행히도 인근에 눈에 띄는 짐승들이 없는 것으로 보아 동물 보호 협회까지 더해질 일은 없을 것 같았다.
 18|
 19|‘야생동물이라 그런지 눈치가 빠르네. 벌써 다 도망친건가?’
 20|
 21|사실 지금은 어떻게 되어도 상관없다.
 22|
 23|굳이 불쌍한 노루 일가족의 터전과 목숨을 빼앗고 싶지는 않지만, 그보다는 암천의 흉계를 저지하는 것과 다른 이들의 목숨이 더 중요하니까.
 24|
 25|‘만약 내가 느낀 불길함이 사실이라면…….’
 26|
 27|더 이상 머뭇거릴 여유 따위는 없다.
 28|
 29|신속하게 달려가던 나는 십여 장 앞을 가로막은 화염의 벽을 확인하고 허공을 향해 손을 뻗었다.
 30|
 31|‘인벤토리 오픈. 소환.’
 32|
 33|요서부에서 투항할 당시에 백염(白炎)을 꺼내지 않았던 건 옳은 선택이었다.
 34|
 35|압수당했다면 가장 중요한 지금 같은 순간에 사용할 수 없었을 테니까.
 36|
 37|슥.
 38|
 39|손아귀를 가득 채우는 서늘한 감촉. 투명하리만치 새하얀 창날에 사방에서 일렁이는 불꽃이 비친다.
 40|
 41|‘지금.’
 42|
 43|이미 사방이 불바다로 변해 가는 지금, 열양지기를 실어 쏘아 보내는 멍청한 짓 따위는 하지 않았다.
 44|
 45|지금 내게 필요한 것은 강한 힘과 속도. 더불어 간결하면서도 완벽한 동작과 흐름뿐이다.
 46|
 47|쉭!
 48|
 49|짧은 파공성과 함께, 비스듬히 내리그은 창날의 끝에서 뛰쳐나간 광풍(狂風)이 화염을 찢어발겼다.
 50|
 51|화륵, 퍼어어엉!
 52|
 53|폭발음과 함께 열린 길.
 54|
 55|새하얀 터럭 위로 바짝 엎드린 나는, 불길에 가로막혀 잠시 주춤하고 있던 무야호의 귓가에 속삭였다.
 56|
 57|“가자.”
 58|
 59|- 크릉.
 60|
 61|낮은 울음소리로 대답을 대신한 백호가 빛살처럼 신형을 날렸다.
 62|
 63|파도처럼 넘실거리는 화염이 그런 우리의 뒤를 바짝 추격했지만, 이런 혼란 속에서도 녀석은 자신의 목적지를 정확히 알고 있었다.
 64|
 65|파파파팟!
 66|
 67|빠르게 스쳐 지나가는 풍경. 하늘 높이 뜬 달은 구름에 가려져 있고, 그 아래에서 불길을 등진 채 쉼 없이 나아가던 나는 왠지 모를 익숙함에 중얼거렸다.
 68|
 69|“설마…….”
 70|
 71|그리고 다음 순간, 뇌리를 스친 어떤 생각에 나는 문득 입을 다물었다.
 72|
 73|아니, 어쩌면 설마가 아닐 것이다.
 74|
 75|분명 낯설어야 할 이 길과 주위 풍경이 익숙하게 느껴진다는 것은, 단 한 가지 사실만을 의미하니까.
 76|
 77|‘독혈지(毒血地).’
 78|
 79|과거 남만 전체를 공포로 몰아넣었던 오독문의 멸문 이후, 남만의 금지(禁地)로 불리게 된 애뇌산.
 80|
 81|그리고 애뇌산에서도 가장 깊고 은밀한 곳에 위치한 독혈지.
 82|
 83|만일 내 짐작이 맞다면…… 우리는 지금 바로 그 독혈지로 향하고 있다. 어쩌면 남만에서 가장 위험할지도 모르는 그 장소로.
 84|
 85|‘하지만 지금쯤 그곳은 적지 않은 병력들이 지키고 있을 텐데.’
 86|
 87|남만야수궁은 어중이떠중이만 모여 있는 촌구석 문파가 아니다.
 88|
 89|극히 드문 독물인 천년지주가 다섯 마리씩이나 나타나고, 오랜 시간 동안 그 누구도 발견하지 못했던 독혈지가 모습을 드러내자 남만야수궁은 적지 않은 숫자의 병력을 파견했다.
 90|
 91|혹시 남아 있을지도 모를 오독문의 잔재와 위험을 뿌리 뽑기 위함이었다.
 92|
 93|‘아무리 등하불명(燈下不明)을 노렸다고는 해도, 그런 곳으로 숨어들었다고?’
 94|
 95|그리고 내가 떠올린 의문이 해결되기까지는, 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않았다.
 96|
 97|- 크르르…….
 98|
 99|어느 순간 서서히 느려지는 발걸음.
100|
101|무언가를 느끼고 이빨을 드러낸 무야호의 모습에 나는 일이 생겼음을 직감했고, 이내 매캐한 연기 사이로 스며드는 비릿한 냄새가 인간의 혈향(血香)이라는 것을 깨달았다.
102|
103|‘그래. 그렇단 말이지.’
104|
105|내심 중얼거린 나는 독혈지의 입구를 바라보았다. 거대한 괴수의 아가리처럼 벌려져 있는 그곳은, 처음 왔던 그때처럼 알 수 없는 위험으로 가득해 보였다.
106|
107|아니, 어쩌면 그때 이상으로.
108|
109|‘하긴, 쉬웠으면 초절정 등급 퀘스트가 아니지.’
110|
111|어쩐지 일이 생각보다 쉽게 풀린다 싶었다. 하지만 백상과는 다른 의미로, 지금의 나는 돌아가기에는 너무 멀리 왔다.
112|
113|당장 눈앞의 위험을 피해 간다면, 그 뒤에는 더 큰 위험이 들이닥칠 것이다.
114|
115|지금 이 순간조차 산림을 휩쓸며 다가오는 등 뒤의 화염처럼.
116|
117|스윽.
118|
119|무야호의 등에서 내린 나는, 평소 녀석이 좋아하던 턱밑을 살살 긁어 주며 말을 건넸다.
120|
121|“아무래도 우리가 함께하는 건 여기까지인 모양이다. 지난번과 다른 건, 이번에는 돌아오지 않아도 된다는 거야.”
122|
123|- 크릉?
124|
125|“더 늦기 전에 돌아가. 너라면 불길을 뚫고 빠져나갈 수 있을 거다.”
126|
127|- 크르릉…….
128|
129|무야호는 작은 울음소리와 함께 내 눈을 물끄러미 바라보았다.
130|
131|나는 이 영민한 백호의 청백색의 눈동자에 떠오른 갈등과 두려움을 느낄 수 있었다.
132|
133|뛰어난 본능을 지닌 존재답게, 녀석도 이미 짐작하고 있는 듯했다.
134|
135|들어가기는 쉬워도 나가는 것은 어렵다는 걸.
136|
137|어쩌면 두 번 다시 야율목을 보지 못할 수도 있다는 걸.
138|
139|그럼에도 지난번처럼 쉽게 발길을 돌리지 못하는 것은, 그간 나름대로 우리 사이에 정이 쌓였기 때문일 것이다.
140|
141|“나도 죽으러 가는 거 아니다. 그러니 걱정하지 말고 먼저 떠나. 네 주인이 기다리고 있을 테니.”
142|
143|안심시키는 말과 함께 부드럽게 목덜미를 쓸어 주자, 그제야 천천히 고개를 끄덕인 무야호가 잠시 멈춰 있던 신형을 날렸다.
144|
145|- 크아아앙!
146|
147|쉬이익!
148|
149|아직 불길이 미치지 않은 언덕이 아닌, 독혈지의 입구를 향해서.
150|
151|“야! 야 인마!”
152|
153|당황 섞인 외침을 토해 냈지만 이미 붙잡기에는 늦은 상황.
154|
155|이 예기치 못한 일에 잠깐 몸이 굳은 그때, 우렁찬 포효와 함께 희뿌연 독무(毒霧) 사이로 닥돌했던 백호가 비틀비틀 걸어 나왔다.
156|
157|- 크륵. 쿨럭.
158|
159|“……피독주 줄까?”
160|
161|멈칫하며 내 시선을 피한 백호가, 슬그머니 고개를 끄덕였다.
162|
163|
164|
165|* * *
166|
167|
168|
169|무야호는 내가 생각했던 것 이상으로 독혈지에 빠르게 적응했다.
170|
171|피독주를 물다 못해 꿀꺽 삼켜 버린 녀석은 기민한 반사신경으로 곳곳에서 밀려오는 독물들을 처리했고, 경신법 좀 익혔다는 절정 고수들도 주저할 만큼 큰 폭을 가진 늪을 단 한 번의 도약으로 뛰어넘었다.
172|
173|그러나 점점 더 깊숙한 곳으로 향할수록, 녀석의 움직임과 호흡 역시 조심스러워졌다.
174|
175|솨아아아.
176|
177|독혈지 내부를 잠식한 독무로 인해 쉽사리 분간할 수 없는 시야. 알 수 없는 무언가가 풀을 스치는 소리와 물 떨어지는 소리만 드문드문 들려올 뿐, 사방은 소름이 끼칠 만큼 적막했다.
178|
179|‘지난번에 야수묘왕과 함께 왔을 때도 이 정도는 아니었는데.’
180|
181|입구에서 혈향을 맡았을 때부터 느꼈지만, 이건 결코 좋은 징조가 아니다.
182|
183|아마도…… 아니, 상당히 높은 확률로 며칠 전 남만야수궁이 독혈지에 파견한 이들은 이미 이 세상 사람이 아닐지도 모르겠다는 생각이 문득 뇌리를 스쳤다.
184|
185|‘만약 그렇다면, 분명 그놈 짓이겠지.’
186|
187|이름과 별호도, 얼굴도 드러나지 않은 초절정 고수.
188|
189|촌각도 걸리지 않은 짧은 시간 동안 요서부를 피로 물들이고 흑웅과 요희를 납치해 간 그놈이라면 충분히 벌일 수 있는 일이다.
190|
191|어쩌면 놈이 아니라, ‘놈들’일 가능성도 농후했다.
192|
193|암천(暗天).
194|
195|마교의 뒤를 이어 등장한 놈들의 전력은, 지금까지 드러난 것만으로도 무시무시한 수준이다.
196|
197|특히 내가 직접 부딪혀 보기까지 한 혈주와 서천마군의 무위는…… 시스템을 바탕삼아 수많은 단련과 사선을 넘나드는 전투로 급성장한 지금의 나조차 감히 승리를 장담할 수 없을 정도다.
198|
199|‘비록 겪어 본 적은 없지만, 남천마후 역시 놈들과 비교해도 떨어지지 않을 만한 실력자일 테고.’
200|
201|그렇기에 홀로 적지로 향하고 있는 나로서는 더욱 긴장될 수밖에 없었다.
202|
203|혈주와 맞닥트렸을 때는 검성(劍星) 매종학이 있었고, 그 어느 때보다 죽음에 가까웠던 서천마군과의 결전에서는 적천강의 도움이 있었으니까.
204|
205|‘하지만 이곳에 남천마후가 있다면…….’
206|
207|내가 살아서 동료들을, 가족들을 다시 만날 수 있을까.
208|
209|툭.
210|
211|그리고 인지하지도 못한 사이에 맺힌 식은땀 한 방울이, 목덜미를 타고 미끄러지던 바로 그 순간이었다.
212|
213|할짝.
214|
215|쓰라릴 만큼 까슬까슬한 감촉.
216|
217|혓바닥으로 목덜미를 핥아 준 백호가 천연덕스럽게 모른 척하는 모습을 보니, 나도 모르게 피식 실소가 흘러나왔다.
218|
219|“긴장하지 말라고?”
220|
221|- 그르릉.
222|
223|별것 아닌 일이지만 이상하게 마음이 편안해진다.
224|
225|생각해 보면 지금까지 죽을 위기를 수두룩하게 겪었는데, 여기까지 와 놓고 새삼 식은땀을 흘리다니.
226|
227|이렇게 긴장했다간 오히려 몸이 굳어 제대로 싸우기조차 힘들다.
228|
229|‘그래, 시발. 어차피 한두 번이냐.’
230|
231|열화문의 계승자이자 화왕의 후인이 갖춰야 할 필수 덕목, 노빠꾸 정신을 몸과 마음에 되새긴 나는 독무를 향해 일장(一掌)을 뻗었다.
232|
233|퍼엉!
234|
235|적막함을 깨트리는 파공성.
236|
237|독과는 극상성인 열양지기. 그중에서도 강맹하기 이루 말할 수 없는 화염신장(火焰神掌)의 열기가 뻗어 나가자, 짙은 독무가 산산이 부서져 흩어지고 어두웠던 독혈지가 붉게 물든다.
238|
239|스스스슥!
240|
241|황급히 빛과 열기를 피해 움직이는 희한한 형태의 독물들.
242|
243|마침내 환하게 드러난 미로처럼 얽힌 길을 노려보던 나는, 공력을 실어 포효하듯 내질렀다.
244|
245|“나와! 이 개새끼들아!”
246|
247|- 크아아아앙!
248|
249|
250|
251|* * *
252|
253|
254|
255|도대체 어떻게 된 일일까.
256|
257|어느 순간, 불현듯 정신을 차린 요희(妖姬)는 한 치 앞도 분간할 수 없는 어둠 속에서 눈을 깜빡였다.
258|
259|“아.”
260|
261|언제나 고혹적이던 목소리는 반쯤 쉬어 있었고, 오랫동안 움직이지 않았던 탓인지 전신 곳곳이 욱신거렸다.
262|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P4]
If the Scorching Hell described in Buddhism existed, I imagined it would look something like this.

[P5]
Ash swirled through acrid smoke. Flames rolled like waves, devouring everything in their path.

[P6]
*Crack. Rumble!*

*If that sense of dread is right…*

[P15]
*Open Inventory. Summon.*

[P16]

[P17]
*Shing.*

[P18]

[P19]
*Now.*

[P20]

[P21]

[P22]
*Whoosh!*

[P23]

[P24]
*Fwoosh! Boom!*

[P25]
The explosion opened a path.

[P26]

[P27]
“Let’s go.”

[P28]
- *Grrr.*

[P29]

[P30]

[P31]
*Papat!*

[P32]
The scenery flashed past. Clouds hid the moon high overhead. As we raced on with the fire at our backs, something about the path struck me as familiar.

[P33]
“Don’t tell me…”

[P34]
A thought flashed through my mind, and I fell silent.

[P35]

[P36]
*The Poisonblood Grounds.*

[P37]
After the Five Poisons Sect, which had once terrorized all of Nanman, was destroyed, Ailao Mountain became known as one of Nanman’s forbidden lands.

[P38]
And the Poisonblood Grounds lay in its deepest, most secluded reaches.

[P39]
If my guess was right, that was exactly where we were headed. To what might be the most dangerous place in Nanman.

[P40]
*But there should be plenty of troops guarding it by now.*

[P41]
The Nanman Beast Palace wasn’t some backwater sect full of riffraff.

[P42]
When five Thousand-Year Spiders—venomous beasts so rare they were almost unheard of—appeared, and the Poisonblood Grounds emerged after going undiscovered for so long, the Palace had sent a sizable force to root out any surviving remnants of the Five Poisons Sect and whatever dangers remained.

[P43]
*Even if they were trying to hide right under the Palace’s nose, they went in there?*

[P44]
I didn’t have to wait long for an answer.

[P45]
- *Grrrr…*

[P46]
Muyaho gradually slowed. It bared its teeth at something I couldn’t see, and I knew at once that something had happened. Then I caught the smell seeping through the acrid smoke.

[P47]
Human blood.

[P48]
*I see. So that’s how it is.*

[P49]
I looked toward the entrance to the Poisonblood Grounds. It gaped like the maw of a gigantic monster, full of the same unknown dangers I’d sensed on my first visit.

[P50]
No. Perhaps it was worse now.

[P51]
*Well, if it were easy, it wouldn’t be a Supreme Peak-grade Quest.*

[P52]
I’d started to think things were going more smoothly than expected. But like Baeksang—though for a very different reason—I’d come too far to turn back.

[P53]
If I avoided the danger in front of me, something worse would come rushing up behind me. Just like the flames sweeping through the forest at my back.

[P54]
*Rustle.*

[P55]
I climbed down from Muyaho’s back and gently scratched under its chin, where it liked it.

[P56]
“Looks like this is where we part ways. Unlike last time, you don’t have to come back for me.”

[P57]
- *Grrr?*

[P58]
“Go back before it’s too late. You can make it through the flames.”

[P59]
- *Grrrr…*

[P60]
Muyaho gave a soft growl and gazed into my eyes.

[P61]
I could see conflict and fear in the intelligent White Tiger’s blue-white eyes. With instincts like its, it must have guessed already.

[P62]
Getting in would be easy. Getting out would be hard.

[P63]
It might never see Yayul Mok again.

[P64]

[P65]
“I’m not going in there to die. Don’t worry about me. Go on—your master’s waiting.”

[P66]
I stroked the back of its neck. At last, Muyaho gave a slow nod and sprang forward.

[P67]
- *GRAAAWR!*

[P68]
*Whoosh!*

[P69]
Not toward the hill the flames had yet to reach, but straight for the entrance to the Poisonblood Grounds.

[P70]
“Hey! Hey, you idiot!”

[P71]
I shouted, but it was too late to catch it.

[P72]
I froze at the unexpected turn of events. With a mighty roar, the White Tiger charged headlong into the pale Poison Mist—then staggered back out.

[P73]
- *Krrk. Cough.*

[P74]
“…Want a poison-warding pearl?”

[P75]
Muyaho paused, avoided my eyes, and gave a furtive nod.

[P76]
* * *

[P77]
Muyaho adapted to the Poisonblood Grounds much faster than I’d expected.

[P78]
Not content to hold the poison-warding pearl in its mouth, it swallowed the thing whole. Its quick reflexes let it deal with the venomous beasts coming at us from all sides, and it cleared a stretch of swamp so wide that even Peak masters trained in movement techniques would have hesitated to cross it—all in a single leap.

[P79]
But the deeper we went, the more cautious its movements and breathing became.

[P80]
*Whooosh…*

[P81]
Poison Mist filled the grounds, making it hard to see. Something brushed through the grass. Water dripped somewhere out of sight. Apart from those occasional sounds, everything was quiet enough to make my skin crawl.

[P82]
*It wasn’t this bad when I came here with the Beast Miao King.*

[P83]
I’d known something was wrong from the moment I smelled blood at the entrance.

[P84]
A thought crossed my mind. Perhaps… No, there was a good chance the Palace warriors sent here a few days ago were already dead.

[P85]
*If they are, that bastard probably did it.*

[P86]
A Supreme Peak master whose name, sobriquet, and face remained unknown. Someone who had drenched the Western Yao Estate in blood and abducted Heugung and Yohi in mere moments was more than capable of it.

[P87]
And there was a good chance it wasn’t just one bastard.

[P88]
Dark Heaven.

[P89]
Even what they’d revealed of their strength so far was terrifying. They had emerged in the wake of the Demonic Cult, and I’d personally faced the Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

[P90]
Their martial prowess was such that even now, after growing rapidly through the System, relentless training, and countless life-or-death battles, I couldn’t count on beating them.

[P91]
*I haven’t fought the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, but I doubt she’s any weaker.*

[P92]
No wonder I was tense, heading into enemy territory alone.

[P93]
When I’d encountered the Blood Lord, Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had been there. And when I’d come closer to death than ever before in my battle with the Western Heaven Demon Lord, Jeok Cheongang had helped me.

[P94]
*But if the Southern Heaven Demon Empress is here…*

[P95]
Would I live to see my companions and family again?

[P96]
*Drip.*

[P97]
A bead of cold sweat I hadn’t noticed forming slid down the back of my neck.

[P98]
*Lick.*

[P99]
Something rough enough to sting swept over my skin.

[P100]
The White Tiger had licked the back of my neck. Now it was pretending nothing had happened. I let out a quiet laugh.

[P101]
“Telling me not to be nervous?”

[P102]
- *Grrrr.*

[P103]
It was such a small thing, but somehow it put me at ease.

[P104]
I’d faced death more times than I could count. After coming this far, what was I doing breaking into a cold sweat? If I let myself tense up, I’d be too stiff to fight properly.

[P105]
*Yeah, fuck it. It’s not like this is my first time.*

[P106]
I called to mind the no-brakes mentality essential to the successor of the Fire Gate Clan and the heir of the Fire King, then thrust a palm toward the Poison Mist.

[P107]
*Boom!*

[P108]
The sound of displaced air shattered the silence.

[P109]
Scorching Yang Qi was poison’s natural enemy. The fierce heat of Flame Divine Palm surged forward, breaking the thick mist apart and staining the dark Poisonblood Grounds red.

[P110]
*Hssssss!*

[P111]
Strangely shaped venomous beasts scurried away from the light and heat.

[P112]
The tangled, maze-like paths finally lay exposed. I glared into them, put internal energy behind my voice, and roared.

[P113]
“Come out, you fucking bastards!”

[P114]
- *GRAAAAAAWR!*

[P115]
* * *

[P116]
What had happened?

[P117]
Yohi came to her senses and blinked into darkness so deep she couldn’t see an inch in front of her.

[P118]
“Ah.”

[P119]
Her usually alluring voice was half-hoarse. Her body ached all over, perhaps from lying still for so long.

[P120]
Then fragments of memory began to return.

[P121]
“……!”

[P122]
Her heart lurched. Her body, relaxed for a moment, went rigid as stone.

[P123]
Unbelievable images flashed before her eyes.

[P124]
Screams. Corpses. Blood.

[P125]
And the face of the one person responsible for it all.

[P126]
She was about to scream when a voice, carefully hushed, came from the darkness.

[P127]
“Calm yourself, Yohi.”

[P128]
“Gasp…!”

[P129]
“Don’t be frightened. It’s me.”

[P130]
Yohi barely swallowed her scream and tried to steady her pounding heart.

[P131]
As her eyes adjusted to the dark, a familiar figure came into view.

[P132]
“Heugung? Is that really you, big brother?”

[P133]
“It is. Don’t you remember?”

[P134]
It took her a moment to piece her memories back together. She recalled Heugung resisting *him* to the very end.

[P135]
“I forgot for a moment. But why are you speaking so differently…?”

[P136]
Heugung had been waiting not far away in the darkness for her to wake. He gave her a bitter smile.

[P137]
“There are reasons. Things I couldn’t easily tell even you.”

[P138]
His tone was so courteous. Yohi was used to seeing Heugung grin foolishly and call her “my dear”; this side of him felt strange. But it wasn’t what mattered now.

[P139]
“Where are we? Wh-where is that man?”

[P140]
“I don’t know either. I woke up here.”

[P141]
Iron chains bound her body, and her internal energy wouldn’t budge.

[P142]
Yohi searched the darkness around her in despair. Then came a heavy noise, and faint light poured in.

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
